A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DisentangledSSL research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including v2's added appendices I and J.

before.justification: Sections 3 and Appendix H report original simulations, MultiBench prediction results, biological retrieval and reconstruction experiments, and counterfactual-generation results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds SimMMDG comparisons, synthetic noise experiments, and MultiBench hyperparameter ablations.

M1.justification: The two-stage training procedure, representation conditioning, information objectives, vMF modeling, InfoNCE losses, and orthogonality penalty remain unchanged. Appendix I supplies pseudocode for the existing procedure.

E1.justification: The five MultiBench datasets, RXRX19a, LINCS, and their tasks are retained. Appendix H.1 adds synthetic input conditions with small, medium, and large noise through Gaussian noise and dropout variation; the expanded dataset descriptions introduce no additional datasets.

E2.justification: SimMMDG is added to the synthetic comparisons in Figure 4b and Appendix H.1's Figures 8–9. It is not added to the MultiBench or biological comparison tables, whose comparator membership remains unchanged.

E3.justification: New experiments vary synthetic corruption and MultiBench beta/lambda settings. Table 1 also changes its reporting rule to the best shared, specific, or combined representation for each applicable method. Retained splits, encoders, dimensions, and metrics are unchanged; this does not establish reruns of existing configurations.

E4.justification: Figure 11 adds a noise-severity analysis, while Table 5 adds direct beta/lambda ablations across all five MultiBench datasets. These substantially extend examination of the control parameters into real-data sensitivity and noise dependence, beyond v1's existing synthetic sweeps, mixed-entanglement analysis, and biological beta-zero comparison.

E5.justification: Both versions report three-seed synthetic averages and three-seed means and standard deviations for MultiBench and biological experiments. The new ablation table follows the existing practice; no increased run count, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial result sets for SimMMDG, noise sensitivity, and MultiBench ablations. For example, Table 5 newly reports MIMIC combined accuracy of 62.70 (0.63) at beta=100 and lambda=0.001, alongside the retained 66.44 (0.31) at beta=1. Existing benchmark and biological results are unchanged; Table 1 reselects previously reported representations.

T1.justification: Appendix B, Equation (6), corrects the IB relevance term from I(Z1; Z2) to I(Z1; X2), matching the preceding formulation. The propositions, assumptions, and proofs are otherwise retained; Appendix J summarizes existing notation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about controlled shared/specific disentanglement, optimality when MNI is unattainable, and empirical advantages across the existing application families.

C2.justification: v2 interprets lower noise as easing the expressivity–redundancy tradeoff and explains MultiBench parameter sensitivity through discarded information, cross-modal contradictions, and stronger independence constraints. The high-beta representation-collapse limitation was already discussed in v1.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access link, a reproducibility statement, PyTorch-style pseudocode in Appendix I, dataset modality/label descriptions in H.2, and SimMMDG tuning details. Existing hardware, architecture, and default hyperparameter disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: Section 4 and the references add Dong et al. (2023) and Li et al. (2022), covering multimodal domain generalization and shared/specific information across image views. The broader positioning relative to information bottleneck and disentanglement research remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized introduction edits, adds explanatory footnotes, moves the experimental guiding questions into Appendix H, and adds the reproducibility statement and appendices I–J. Most prose and the main narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Selected displays are revised: Figure 2 is redrawn, simulation plots gain SimMMDG curves, and Table 1 is condensed. New displays include Figure 5 redisplaying existing accuracies, Figure 11, ablation Table 5, Algorithm 1, and notation Table 7. Existing counterfactual results are retained as Table 6.

improvement.justification: The new noise and MultiBench ablations strengthen scrutiny of the control parameters, and Table 1 uses a more consistent comparison rule. Pseudocode and code-access information improve reproducibility. These are incremental gains over v1's existing evidence; unspecified numerical noise levels and an incorrect reconstruction-gain table reference limit the revision's polish.
